atoms.text: This guide configures the destination bucket app-data-dr in the eu-west-1 region to receive cross-region replicas from app-data-primary for disaster recovery. Versioning must be enabled on both buckets before replication starts. The bucket policy contains one Allow statement that grants s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::app-data-dr/*, and s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::app-data-dr. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/dr-replication-role, which is the role the replication configuration on the source bucket is set to use. The role's trust policy must allow the replication job to assume it, and its permissions policy must allow reading from the source bucket. The role is the identity that signs every write into the destination, so the statement does not need extra source conditions. Objects are written under their original keys, and delete markers are copied when delete marker replication is enabled. After applying the policy, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replication status changes to COMPLETED and that the object appears in app-data-dr.

This guide configures the destination bucket app-data-dr in the eu-west-1 region to receive cross-region replicas from app-data-primary for disaster recovery. Versioning must be enabled on both buckets before replication starts. The bucket policy contains one Allow statement that grants s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::app-data-dr/*, and s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::app-data-dr. The Principal is the service principal vaultsync.amazonaws.com, which is the identity the replication service uses when it writes to the destination. The statement carries an aws:SourceAccount condition of 111122223333 and an ArnLike condition on aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:vaultsync:us-east-1:111122223333:replication-job/app-data-*. These conditions prevent the service from acting on behalf of any other customer's jobs. Objects are written under their original keys, and delete markers are copied when delete marker replication is enabled. After applying the policy, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replication status changes to COMPLETED and that the object appears in app-data-dr.

This guide covers the bucket policy for db-nightly-backups, which stores compressed database snapshots written once per night. The snapshots are uploaded under the prefix snapshots/prod-orders/ using multipart upload. The bucket policy has one Allow statement for s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::db-nightly-backups/snapshots/prod-orders/*. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/orders-db-backup-role, which the backup job assumes at run time. Because the role belongs to a different account than the bucket, the role's own identity policy must also allow the same actions. The statement does not grant s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject, so the backup job cannot read or remove earlier snapshots. Restores are done by a separate administrative role that is covered in a different section. To verify the setup, run the backup job manually and check that a snapshot object with the current date in its key appears under the prefix.

This guide covers the bucket policy for db-nightly-backups, which stores compressed database snapshots written once per night. The snapshots are uploaded under the prefix snapshots/prod-orders/ using multipart upload. The bucket policy has one Allow statement for s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::db-nightly-backups/snapshots/prod-orders/*. The Principal is the service principal snapvault.amazonaws.com, which writes the snapshots when the scheduled backup plan runs. The statement is restricted with an aws:SourceAccount condition of 444455556666 and an aws:SourceArn condition equal to arn:aws:snapvault:us-west-2:444455556666:backup-plan/orders-nightly. The statement does not grant s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject, so the backup service cannot read or remove earlier snapshots. Restores are done by a separate administrative role that is covered in a different section. To verify the setup, run the backup plan manually and check that a snapshot object with the current date in its key appears under the prefix.

This guide describes how to let an archive account receive replicated objects from a production account for long-term durability. The destination bucket is archive-store-eu, owned by account 777788889999, and the source bucket is owned by account 111122223333. The bucket policy includes an Allow statement for s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::archive-store-eu/*. It also includes s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner, so that replicas become owned by the destination account. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/archive-replication-role in the source account. The source account administrator must give this role matching permissions in its identity policy and reference it in the replication rule. The destination bucket should have versioning enabled and the replication rule should filter on the prefix finance/. After you create the rule, replicate an existing object by using a batch copy and verify that its owner in the destination bucket is account 777788889999.

This guide describes how to let an archive account receive replicated objects from a production account for long-term durability. The destination bucket is archive-store-eu, owned by account 777788889999, and the source bucket is owned by account 111122223333. The bucket policy includes an Allow statement for s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::archive-store-eu/*. It also includes s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner, so that replicas become owned by the destination account. The Principal is the service principal vaultsync.amazonaws.com, restricted by an aws:SourceAccount condition of 111122223333 so that only jobs from the production account are accepted. An additional aws:SourceArn condition limits the statement to the replication rule arn:aws:vaultsync:us-east-1:111122223333:replication-rule/finance-archive. The destination bucket should have versioning enabled and the replication rule should filter on the prefix finance/. After you create the rule, replicate an existing object by using a batch copy and verify that its owner in the destination bucket is account 777788889999.

This guide explains how to give a backup copy process read access to a primary bucket so it can copy objects into an offsite vault bucket. The primary bucket is media-primary and the process reads objects under the prefix masters/. The bucket policy on media-primary has one Allow statement for s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::media-primary/masters/*. A second action, s3:ListBucket, is granted on arn:aws:s3:::media-primary with an s3:prefix condition of masters/. The Principal is the IAM user arn:aws:iam::222233334444:user/offsite-copy-agent, whose access keys are stored on the copy host. Rotate those keys at least every 90 days and record the rotation in your change log. The agent writes each object it reads to the vault bucket with its original key and checksum. Confirm the configuration by listing the prefix with the agent's credentials and comparing the vault object count with the source count.

This guide explains how to give a backup copy process read access to a primary bucket so it can copy objects into an offsite vault bucket. The primary bucket is media-primary and the process reads objects under the prefix masters/. The bucket policy on media-primary has one Allow statement for s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::media-primary/masters/*. A second action, s3:ListBucket, is granted on arn:aws:s3:::media-primary with an s3:prefix condition of masters/. The Principal is the service principal offsitecopy.amazonaws.com, which reads the data when a copy job runs. The statement includes aws:SourceAccount set to 222233334444 and an aws:SourceArn condition matching arn:aws:offsitecopy:us-east-1:222233334444:copy-job/media-*. The service writes each object it reads to the vault bucket with its original key and checksum. Confirm the configuration by running a copy job against the prefix and comparing the vault object count with the source count.

This guide covers replication of application audit logs to a compliance bucket named audit-replica, where objects must be retained for disaster recovery. The source bucket receives log files every five minutes under the prefix audit/. The destination bucket policy contains an Allow statement for s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::audit-replica/audit/*. A separate Deny statement rejects any request that does not use TLS by testing aws:SecureTransport. The Principal of the Allow statement is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/audit-log-replicator. The role needs s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and read access on the source bucket in its own identity policy. Replicated objects keep their original storage class unless the rule specifies otherwise. To validate the setup, wait for the next log file to be written and check that the same key exists in audit-replica within the expected delay.

This guide describes the failback step of a disaster recovery plan, in which data is copied from the recovery bucket app-recovery back to the restored primary bucket. The copy reads objects under the prefix restore/ and writes them to the primary bucket with their original keys. The bucket policy on app-recovery has one Allow statement for s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::app-recovery/restore/*. It also grants s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::app-recovery with a prefix condition of restore/. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/failback-operator-role, which the on-call engineer assumes during the recovery event. Session duration for the role should be set to at least four hours to cover large copies. No write or delete actions are granted on app-recovery, so the recovery copy remains unchanged. After failback, compare object counts and checksums between both buckets before redirecting application traffic.

The Principal is the service principal failback.amazonaws.com, which runs the recovery workflow, with aws:SourceAccount set to 555566667777. An aws:SourceArn condition limits the statement to arn:aws:failback:us-west-2:555566667777:recovery-plan/app-primary. No write or delete actions are granted on app-recovery, so the recovery copy remains unchanged. This guide shows how to configure a bucket that stores incremental snapshots of a file share, used to rebuild the share after data loss. The bucket is fileshare-snapshots, and snapshot chunks are stored under the prefix shares/team-docs/chunks/. The bucket policy has one Allow statement for s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::fileshare-snapshots/shares/team-docs/chunks/*. It also grants s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket resource. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/fileshare-snapshot-role, which is attached to the snapshot appliance instances. Reads are required because each incremental snapshot checks existing chunks to avoid uploading duplicates. A condition on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption requires encryption with a customer-managed key for all writes. To test the policy, create a snapshot and verify that new chunk objects appear under the prefix with the expected encryption header.

This guide shows how to configure a bucket that stores incremental snapshots of a file share, used to rebuild the share after data loss. The bucket is fileshare-snapshots, and snapshot chunks are stored under the prefix shares/team-docs/chunks/. The bucket policy has one Allow statement for s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::fileshare-snapshots/shares/team-docs/chunks/*. It also grants s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket resource. The Principal is the service principal sharesnap.amazonaws.com, with aws:SourceAccount set to 888899990000 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:sharesnap:us-east-2:888899990000:share/team-docs. Reads are required because each incremental snapshot checks existing chunks to avoid uploading duplicates. A condition on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption requires encryption with a customer-managed key for all writes. To test the policy, create a snapshot and verify that new chunk objects appear under the prefix with the expected encryption header.

This guide explains how to authorize a manifest-driven batch copy that duplicates objects from inventory-source into a secondary bucket, inventory-secondary, for durability. The job reads a manifest file that lists the keys to copy and then writes each object to the secondary bucket. The bucket policy on inventory-secondary has one Allow statement for s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging and s3:PutObjectAcl on arn:aws:s3:::inventory-secondary/copies/*. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::999900001111:role/batch-copy-execution-role, which is named in the batch job definition. The same role needs s3:GetObject on the source bucket and on the manifest location. Jobs fail with an access denied error in the completion report if any of these permissions are missing. The completion report is written to a separate prefix, reports/, in the source bucket. After the first run, review the report for failed keys and spot-check the checksums of several copied objects.
